title: Game Score System
story: Your indie game needs a score tracking system. Players earn points, beat high scores, and want their names on the leaderboard. Functions make the scoring engine clean and maintainable.
why: Score management is a classic use case for functions: calculate, compare, and display — all separated into focused, reusable units.
analogy: A game score system is like an arcade machine. The coin slot adds value (add_score), the machine checks if you beat the top score (check_high_score), and the marquee shows your name in lights (display_scoreboard).
try_it: Add a `calculate_bonus(score: Int, multiplier: Int) -> Int` function that awards bonus points, and call it when a player beats the high score.
tips: Use `var` for values that change — like the player's score and high score
check_high_score returns a Bool so it can be used directly in an if statement
display_scoreboard is a void function — it prints, doesn't return
Chain score additions: `score = add_score(score, points);` updates the running total
common_mistakes: Using `let` for score when you need to change it — use `var` instead
Forgetting to assign the result of add_score back to the variable
Checking `score >= high_score` when you meant `score > high_score` — different behavior for ties
